skill.name: reviewdog
skill.description: Configure reviewdog to publish security scanner and linter findings as inline CI review feedback across GitHub, GitLab, and local pre-commit workflows.
skill.summary: Integrate multiple security scanners with reviewdog for actionable pull request and local feedback.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, documentation URLs, /dev/null redirection, and references to platform-managed CI tokens. The GitLab template critically downloads a mutable remote installer and pipes it directly to sh. The templates also use predictable temporary files, unpinned CI dependencies, and fail-open secret-scanning patterns.

remediation.issue: The GitLab template executes a mutable remote installer without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Download a pinned release artifact, verify its published checksum or signature, and execute the verified local file.

remediation.issue: CI actions, scanner releases, packages, and container images use mutable versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions to commit SHAs, containers to digests, and packages to reviewed versions. Use automated updates with review.

remediation.issue: Critical Gitleaks commands suppress all nonzero exit statuses.
remediation.suggestion: Distinguish findings from execution errors, require a valid report, and fail the job when Gitleaks cannot complete.

remediation.issue: Gitleaks uses a predictable report path under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary file with mktemp or the CI runner temporary directory, then remove it after processing.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable CI Dependencies Execute in a Privileged Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The GitHub workflow uses a mutable major action tag, requests the latest reviewdog release, and installs unpinned Python packages. Upstream changes can execute before later steps receive a write-capable GitHub token.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mutable action tag, latest version selector, and unpinned package installation are explicit. The workflow also grants pull-request and checks write permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Critical Secret Scans Fail Open
semantic_findings.description: Gitleaks failures are suppressed with true, and missing reports can produce empty findings or skip reviewdog. Scanner crashes can therefore pass the critical secret gate.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each configuration explicitly suppresses the Gitleaks exit status. At least one path substitutes empty findings or skips review processing when output is absent.

content.user_title: Integrate Reviewdog Security Feedback into CI
content.value_statement: Security scanner results are often fragmented across CI logs. This skill helps configure reviewdog to publish focused findings in pull requests and local hooks.
actual_capabilities: Configures reviewdog runners for Bandit, Semgrep, Gitleaks, Hadolint, Checkov, and ShellCheck.
Provides templates for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, pre-commit, and reviewdog configuration.
Selects pull request, check, merge request, or local reporters.
Applies diff filters, severity levels, and failure thresholds to scanner output.
Documents supported formats, custom scanner integration, and CWE mapping.
limitations: Reviewdog and each selected scanner must be installed separately.
Reporter access requires correctly scoped platform tokens and repository permissions.
Scanner output compatibility can change across tool versions.
The setup and security suite scripts referenced in the guide are not included.

use_cases.title: Add Pull Request Security Comments
use_cases.description: Publish Bandit and Semgrep findings on changed lines in GitHub pull requests.

use_cases.title: Standardize GitLab Security Gates
use_cases.description: Combine multiple scanners into consistent merge request discussions and blocking thresholds.

use_cases.title: Run Local Pre-Commit Reviews
use_cases.description: Surface security and lint findings before code reaches the remote repository.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Local Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure reviewdog for [language] using [scanner]. Use the local reporter, scan changed files, and explain required dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Add a GitHub Actions Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions reviewdog workflow for [scanners]. Use least-privilege permissions, pinned dependencies, and pull request annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Build a GitLab Security Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitLab CI reviewdog pipeline for [scanners]. Block [severity] findings and report lower severities without suppressing scanner failures.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Tool Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reviewdog policy for [repository]. Define reporters, diff filters, severity mappings, failure behavior, token permissions, and verified dependency versions.

output_examples.input: Configure Bandit for local Python review.
output: A local reporter configuration for Bandit findings.
A changed-line filter and blocking error threshold.
Required reviewdog and Bandit installation steps.

output_examples.input: Add Semgrep and Gitleaks to GitHub pull requests.
output: A pull request workflow with minimal write permissions.
Separate critical and warning review channels.
Pinned dependencies and fail-closed scanner handling.

output_examples.input: Integrate a custom scanner with reviewdog.
output_examples.output: A format selection, field mapping, reporter choice, severity policy, and validation checklist for the custom scanner.

best_practices: Pin actions, packages, installers, and container images to reviewed immutable versions.
Grant reporter tokens only the repository permissions required for comments and checks.
Fail closed when a critical scanner crashes or produces an invalid report.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installation scripts directly into a shell.
Do not suppress every scanner error with unconditional success handling.
Do not expose broad write tokens to unpinned tools or untrusted pull request workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill run security scanners itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates for connecting installed scanners to reviewdog.

faq.question: Which code hosting platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The included guidance covers GitHub and GitLab, with reference material for Bitbucket and Gerrit reporters.

faq.question: Can reviewdog block a pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure failure thresholds and required CI checks so selected finding levels block merging.

faq.question: Which scanners are included in the templates?
faq.answer: Examples cover Bandit, Semgrep, Gitleaks, Hadolint, Checkov, and ShellCheck.

faq.question: Does reviewdog remove scanner false positives?
faq.answer: No. It filters and reports findings, while scanner rules and suppressions control false positives.

faq.question: How should CI tokens be configured?
faq.answer: Store tokens in platform secrets, grant minimal permissions, and avoid exposing them to untrusted or mutable dependencies.
